Kind regards,
[Your name]

Answer:
Dear Ms Norr,

I am writing regarding the rent charged for 1 to 8 June for the flat I rented from you.

As you know, I removed all of my belongings and vacated the flat on 31 May, and I did not live there at any point in June. The only reason the keys were returned on 8 June rather than earlier is that this was the first date I was able to get to your office to hand them over in person. The flat was empty and unused for the entire period in question.

I understand that our agreement states that rent continues until all keys are returned. However, given that I had fully moved out by 31 May and the flat was not occupied during June, I would be grateful if you would consider refunding the rent charged for 1 to 8 June as a gesture of goodwill. If a refund is agreed, please send it to my usual account, the one from which my rent payments were made.

Thank you for your consideration, and for your help during my tenancy. I would appreciate a reply at your convenience.

Yours sincerely,
[Your name]
[Former address]
[Contact details]

Note: By your own account the agreement runs rent until key return, so the 1–8 June charge appears to be correct; I've framed the letter as a goodwill request rather than a claim of entitlement, since asserting otherwise could weaken your position.
